Explanatory Remarks
  The present text is edited to facilitate word-searches. The text is based on the manuscript of the transliteration of the AbhisamAcArika-Dharma of the MahAsAGghika-LokottaravAdins. Grammatical errors and the like have been left uncorrected, but preferred readings are occasionally given for conspicuous scribal errors.
  The symbols and editorial features are as follows:
(1) The letters between ( ) indicate that they should be supplied.
(2) The letters which seem to be wrongly written are underlined. Immediately after them suggestion is supplied between ( ).
(3) Letters in blue and underlined are to be omitted. No suggestion is supplied after them. This applies to the omission of the virAma.
(4) The letters between [ ] indicate that they are obscure.
(5) An illegible character (akXaras) is indicated by one "+".
(6) Symbols which seem to indicate virama are substituted by comma (" , ").
(7) Symbols which seem to be SiddhaM, etc., are substituted by " * ".
(8) Cancellations in the Ms. are not indicated.
(9) J. refers to the Jinananda edition.
(10) Compounds in which hiatus appears are hyphened.

Abhisamācārikadharma

(I.p.43)
<s>Abhisamācārikadharma</s> (Rules of Proper Conduct)

children.translated_text:
and the remainder by way of frequent recitation. Now if the <s>Saṅgha</s> has not assembled, the elder of the <s>Saṅgha</s> should announce wherever it will take place: 'Venerable ones, today is the <s>Saṅgha</s>'s <s>Poṣadha</s> — whether on the fourteenth, the fifteenth, or a conjunction <s>Poṣadha</s>. It will take place at such-and-such a place — in the meditation hall, or the assembly hall, or the circular pavilion — before the meal or after the meal. Let the venerable ones proceed there, for the announcement has now been made by me.' One should remain seated at a convenient place.
  Then, having made preparations, one should go to the <s>Poṣadha</s> site. It should be sprinkled, swept, and cow-dung paste should be applied. Seats should be arranged. If there are means, the voting sticks should be washed with scented water and strewn with flowers. The elder of the <s>Saṅgha</s> should know: 'Who will distribute the voting sticks? Who will collect them? Who will recite the <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s> (monastic code)? Who will dedicate the merit? Who will give the discourse?' Whoever is capable should be requested: 'You distribute the voting sticks. You collect the voting sticks. You recite the <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s>. You speak. You give the discourse. You dedicate the merit.' The one so requested should distribute the voting sticks. The second should collect them. It is not proper for the one distributing the voting sticks to distribute them without having washed his hands.

children.text: nāpi kṣamati / oguṇṭhikāyakṛtena upānahā(2a2)rūḍhena vā śalākāṃ
children.translated_text: It is also not proper to distribute the voting sticks with the head covered or while wearing sandals.

bhavati / dāyakadānapati paripṛcchitavyā / kim vasiṣyatha atha
children.translated_text: Rather, having washed the hands, having removed the head covering, having taken off the sandals, with one shoulder bared, the voting sticks should be distributed. And also the one receiving the voting sticks — it is not proper to receive the voting sticks with the head covered or while wearing sandals. Rather, with one shoulder bared, having washed the hands, having removed the head covering, having taken off the sandals, the voting sticks should be received. should be established. The charitable gift should be acknowledged with gratitude. They should be shown, instructed, encouraged, delighted, and urged on with a talk on the <s>Dharma</s>. Now if they say 'We will stay,' it should be said: 'Go outside for a moment, then come back; the <s>Bhikṣusaṅgha</s> will now perform the <s>Poṣadha</s>.' When the lay donors and patrons have gone out, then the reciter of the <s>sūtra</s> should know:
  If it is not excessively cold, not excessively hot, the monasteries are not very far apart, the monks are neither weakened by old age nor weakened by illness, and there is no danger of lions, tigers, or thieves, and the monks are comfortably seated — if they wish to hear the <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s> in full, the <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s> should be recited in full. But if it is excessively cold or excessively hot, the monks are weakened by old age or weakened by illness, there is danger of lions, tigers, or thieves, and the monks do not wish to hear the <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s> in full — then having recited the four <s>Pārājika</s> rules in abbreviated form, and the remainder by way of frequent recitation and verses, thereafter it should be done as is comfortable.
  Now if it is an all-night observance, then the request should be made: 'You shall speak' —

I.1 Ms.1b1 (J.1.1); Ch.499a22
  * Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>. Beginning of the <s>Abhisamācārika</s> (rules of proper conduct).
  The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) dwells in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, the teacher of gods and humans. Having given the <s>nidāna</s> (introduction) in full, now it is the <s>Saṅgha</s>'s <s>Poṣadha</s> (observance day). The venerable <s>Nandana</s> is the elder of the <s>Saṅgha</s>, <s>Upanandana</s> is the second elder. The lay donors and patrons ask: "Noble ones, is the <s>Bhikṣusaṅgha</s> (community of monks) complete?" They said: "No, long-lived ones." "Who then has not come?" The monks said: "The elder of the <s>Saṅgha</s> has not come." Then they express displeasure: "Look, sirs, we have set aside our work and come. We would pay respect at the feet of the complete <s>Saṅgha</s>. We would establish our charitable gifts. Yet the elder of the <s>Saṅgha</s> has not come!" He then came afterwards, recited the four <s>Pārājika</s> (defeat) rules in abbreviated form, did not dedicate the merit, did not give a discourse, got up, and left. The junior monks ask: "Venerable one, did the elder of the <s>Saṅgha</s> not come?" The monks said: "He came and he left." Those junior monks also said: "Neither the coming nor the going of the elder of the <s>Saṅgha</s> was noticed." The monks reported this matter to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Summon <s>Nandana</s>." He was then summoned. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Is it true, <s>Nandana</s>, that the <s>Saṅgha</s>'s <s>Poṣadha</s> was conducted in this manner?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> then related all this in detail. The junior monks express displeasure: "Neither the coming nor the going of the elder of the <s>Saṅgha</s> was noticed." He said: "Yes, <s>Bhagavān</s>."
  The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Therefore, the elder of the <s>Saṅgha</s> should conduct himself in this manner at the <s>Poṣadha</s>. How then should the elder of the <s>Saṅgha</s> conduct himself at the <s>Poṣadha</s>? On whichever day the <s>Saṅgha</s>'s <s>Poṣadha</s> falls, on that day the elder of the <s>Saṅgha</s> should know: 'Will today's <s>Poṣadha</s> of the <s>Saṅgha</s> be on the fourteenth, the fifteenth, or a conjunction <s>Poṣadha</s>?' 'What is the pre-meal time? What is the post-meal time?' 'At how many shadow-lengths of a man will it take place, and where? In the meditation hall, or the assembly hall,

Whatever is comfortable should be done. 'May the venerable ones rejoice!' Thus should the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder conduct [himself] at the <s>poṣadha</s> (observance day). If he does not so conduct [himself], he transgresses the rules of proper conduct (<s>abhisamācārika dharma</s>). ////

children.translated_text: [yet] the second elder does not come.' Then, having waited for just a moment and having made their offering, they left. He [the second elder] came when it was too late. The <s>saṃgha</s>-elder grumbles: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> gives disciplinary action to us, [while] the second elder gets off scot-free.' The <s>bhikṣus</s> reported this matter to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Summon <s>Upanandana</s>.' He was summoned. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Is it true, <s>Upanandana</s>, that thus [it was] at the <s>saṃgha</s>'s <s>poṣadha</s>?' He [<s>Upanandana</s>] reported the entire matter in full to the <s>Bhagavān</s> — even that the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder grumbles: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> gives disciplinary action to us, [while] the second elder gets off scot-free.' He said: 'Yes, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Therefore, thus should the second elder conduct [himself] at the <s>poṣadha</s>. And how should the second elder conduct [himself] at the <s>poṣadha</s>? On whichever day it is the <s>saṃgha</s>'s <s>poṣadha</s>, if the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder is not able, the second elder should know: Is today's <s>poṣadha</s> of the <s>saṃgha</s> on the fourteenth, or the fifteenth, or is it a junction-<s>poṣadha</s>? Will there be a night-<s>poṣadha</s> or a day-<s>poṣadha</s>? Before the meal or after the meal? Where will it be? — in the assembly hall, or the meditation hall, or the circular pavilion, or the open clearing, or the seating area. Wherever it will be, [the second elder] should announce: 'Venerable one, today is the <s>saṃgha</s>'s <s>poṣadha</s>, on the fourteenth or the fifteenth.' Now, if the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder is not able, the second elder should have the <s>poṣadha</s> site sprinkled as a matter of course, should have it swept, should have cow-dung applied, should have the seats arranged. If he has the means, the counting-sticks should be washed with scented water, [the site] should be strewn with flowers. If the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder is not able, the second elder should know: who will distribute the counting-sticks, who will collect the counting-sticks, who will recite the <s>Prātimokṣa-sūtra</s> (monastic code), who will speak, who will dedicate the merit, who will give the discourse. Whoever is capable should be requested: 'You will distribute the counting-sticks, you will collect them,

(I.p.48) I.3 Ms.3a6 (J. 8.14); Ch.499c14 — The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) was dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>. The Teacher of gods and humans, having given the background in detail: Now it was the <s>Saṃgha</s>'s <s>Poṣadha</s> (observance day). The venerable <s>Nandana</s>, the senior monk of the <s>Saṃgha</s>, and <s>Upanandana</s>, the second senior monk, had arrived. [But some] monks did not come to the assembly hall. The lay donors asked: 'Venerable sirs, is the <s>Bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> (community of monks) complete?' The monks said: 'No, long-lived ones, someone has not come.' The monks said: 'These monks do not come to the assembly hall.' Then they complained: 'We have left our various tasks and come; we will pay homage to the feet of the complete [assembly]; we will establish the gift of <s>Dharma</s>. Yet these venerable ones do not come to the assembly hall.' The senior monk and the second senior monk were displeased: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> gives us disciplinary action, but these are silent monks.' The monks reported this matter [to the <s>Bhagavān</s>]. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Summon the monks.' They were then summoned. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Is it true, monks, that it is now the <s>Saṃgha</s>'s <s>Poṣadha</s>?' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> related the whole matter in detail, up to [the point where] the senior monk and the second senior monk were displeased: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> gives us disciplinary action, but these are silent [monks].' They said: 'Yes, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Therefore, all should conduct themselves thus at the <s>Poṣadha</s>. How then? Thus all should conduct themselves at the <s>Poṣadha</s>. All should know: what day of the fortnight is it today — the first, the second, up to the fifteenth? If anyone asks "Venerable sir, what day is it today?" one should not say [one does not know]. But who will know? It must be written on bamboo strips or reed strips, tied with a cord, and fastened at the gate-room, or the upper hall, or the designated hut. Stakes should be driven in and one should stand at the door. Whoever is on a monthly or fortnightly wandering tour, he should pass along [the information] one by one, daily, as instructed — "what day is it today?" — all should know. Now this is the <s>Saṃgha</s>'s <s>Poṣadha</s>. If the senior monk is not capable, if the second senior monk is not capable, then whoever is capable there, he should

children.translated_text: Having eaten in haste, he [merely] dedicated the merit and did not give a discourse; nor did he show, instruct, encourage, or delight the lay donors with a <s>Dharma</s> talk. Having risen, he left. The junior <s>bhikṣus</s> asked: "Has [the senior] come?" They said: "The <s>saṃgha</s>-elder has come and gone." Now they complained: "Neither the coming nor the going of the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder is noticed." The <s>bhikṣus</s> reported this matter to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Summon <s>Nandana</s>." He was then summoned. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Is it true, <s>Nandana</s>, that thus at the <s>Saṃgha</s>'s external meal — <s>Nandana</s> being the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder and <s>Upanandana</s> the second elder?" Then he related the entire matter in detail to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, up to the point where the junior <s>bhikṣus</s> complained, up to the point where neither the coming nor the going of the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder was noticed. He said: "Yes, <s>Bhagavān</s>." The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Therefore, the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder should conduct himself thus at the meal-gathering. And how should the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder conduct himself at the meal-gathering? The <s>saṃgha</s>-elder should know: whose meal is it today — a both-sided <s>Saṃgha</s> meal, a complete <s>Saṃgha</s> meal, a cell-group meal, or a special-invitation meal — [whether] in the village or in the monastery? Now if someone invites the <s>Saṃgha</s> for a meal in exchange for service, the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder should not accept from anyone [merely] coming and going. Rather, the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder should know who is making the invitation — whether a visitor, a traveler, a householder, a renunciant, a woman, a man, a boy, or a girl. One should ask: 'What is your name? What is your clan? What is the occupation of your parents? Which district? Which house? On which street? Which way does the house face?' — asking with such specific details, only then should [the invitation] be accepted. And [one should] not [say]: 'It has been accepted by me' — [and then] sit wherever one is inclined [to sit]."

I.4 Ms.4a5 (J.12.11); Ch.499c28 — The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, the Teacher of gods and humans. Having given the background in detail: Now it was the <s>Saṃgha</s>'s external meal [distribution]. The venerable <s>Nandana</s>, the senior monk, and <s>Upanandana</s>, the second senior monk, had arrived. The monks had arrived. [But] the senior monk did not come. The rice became cold; the soup became cold; the ghee solidified; the meat solidified; the side-dishes became cold. The lay donors asked: 'Venerable sirs, is the <s>Bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> complete?' They said: 'No, long-lived ones, someone has not come.' They said: 'The senior monk has not come.' Then they complained: 'We have left our various tasks and come; we would serve the complete <s>Bhikṣu-saṃgha</s>.

But if they then say: "Venerable sir, [the food] is being prepared — let the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> enter," then the gong should be struck [to assemble everyone]. If it is winter, one should enter at the proper time — "lest the [meal] time pass." But if it is the hot season, one should enter at the proper time, taking advantage of the cool period.

Now then, as a matter of course, a monthly or fortnightly touring monk should be sent: "Go and find out what is being prepared." For sometimes there might be a birth or a death, a breach [in the wall], a fire, trouble from the royal court, a rogue, a cheat, or a troublemaker — [people who] have invited with the intention of harassment. So [the monk] should go and ask: "Is there such-and-such a named <s>upāsaka</s> (lay follower) here?" If they say: "There is no one of that name among our <s>upāsakas</s>," one should say: "The <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> has been invited by him — is [anything] being readied or cooked?" If they say: "Whose meal? Whose is being readied? Whose is being cooked?" — then one should know: "The <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> has been deceived." Returning, if there is a remedy, the remedy should be accomplished. If there is no remedy [but] there are meals, the meals should be distributed. [If] meals

children.translated_text: [food] should be given as a matter of course. Now if that person is one inexperienced in giving or is stingy, [the matter] should not be overlooked. One should say: "Long-lived one, you must certainly give them their alms-food." Now if the lay donors say: "Take in order," and it is winter, one should say: "No — the <s>Bhagavān</s> has declared in many ways [that] the sick and infirm [should be served first]. Can we [allow] the monastery to become empty?" Time passes quickly [in winter]; "Give [to them]." But if it is summer, or the rainy season, or nighttime, [when] time passes slowly, one should accept in proper order. Then the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder should know on what basis [the food] is given, and accordingly the offering should be requested. [When] the meal is given [and] a large portion has been received, the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder should say: "For everyone, there will be this much and this much." If [the donor] says: "No, venerable sir, it is given thus," one should say: "Give in such a way that it is equal for all." If then [the donor] says: "So it shall be," it should be accepted. But if that person wants only a little, one should say: "Give me a little; below, [give] much." And so on for soup, ghee, meat, side-dishes, and curds. Then it is not proper for the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder, having received the portion, to look at the door, eat while muttering, and rise and go. Rather, one should eat waiting for the full serving of rice and waiting for the full serving of side-dishes; one should not, having eaten, put down the hand and sit [idle], lest they [the junior monks] be embarrassed. Rather, permission should be given [to finish]. When the junior monks are satisfied, when they begin to rinse [their mouths], or drink water, or

children.translated_text: "May this boy be destined for the auspicious path; may he survive seven nights by the love of a thumb[-sized infant]; may dogs and jackals leap over him; and may crows carry off the filth of his eyes." — The merit-dedication should not be pronounced in this way.

Now if it is the rainy season, one should enter at the proper time, taking advantage of breaks in the rain — "lest the time pass." If there is no [clear] announcement and the time is long and one wishes to go somewhere, a certain <s>bhikṣu</s> should be told: "Go to such-and-such a family; when [the food] is ready, send word for me." And [one should] not [then say]: "It has been arranged by me."

atha khalu dakṣiṇā ādiśitavyā /
  ayaṃ kumāro śaraṇaṃ upetu
  buddhaṃ vipaśyiñ ca śikhi(ñ) ca viśvabhuṃ
  krakucchanda konākamuniñ ca kāśyapaṃ
  mahāyaśaṃ śākyamuniñ ca gautamaṃ /
  etehi buddhehi maharddhikehi
  (5b2)ye devatā santi abhiprasannā
  tā naṃ rakṣaṃtu tā ca naṃ pālayantu
  yathā naṃ icchati mātā yathā naṃ icchati pitā
  ato śreyataro bhotu kumāro kulavarddhano /
  evaṃ dakṣiṇā ādiśitavyā /
children.translated_text:
Now then, the merit-dedication (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) should be pronounced [thus]:
'May this boy take refuge
in <s>Buddha</s> <s>Vipaśyin</s>, <s>Śikhin</s>, <s>Viśvabhū</s>,
<s>Krakucchanda</s>, <s>Konākamuni</s>, and <s>Kāśyapa</s>,
and the greatly renowned <s>Śākyamuni</s> <s>Gautama</s>.
By these <s>Buddhas</s> of great supernatural power,
whatever deities are well-disposed [to him],
may they protect him, may they guard him,
as his mother wishes for him, as his father wishes for him —
may the boy be ever more auspicious, an increaser of the family.'
Thus should the merit-dedication be pronounced.

children.text:
atha dāni mṛtakaṃ bhavati / nāyaṃ kṣamati / evaṃ dakṣiṇā ādiśituṃ
adya te sudivasaṃ sumahābalaṃ

  adya te suvihite suvihitehi /
  dakṣiṇā agrabhājanaga(5b3)gatā virocati /
  (J.19) nāyaṃ evaṃ dakṣiṇā ādiśitavyā /
children.translated_text:
Now when there is a death, this [formula] is not appropriate. The merit-dedication should not be pronounced thus:
'Today is an auspicious day of great power for you,
a fortunate moment and [good] hour — you have set forth.
Today, well-prepared, by the well-prepared,
the merit-dedication gone to the foremost vessel shines forth.'
This merit-dedication should not be pronounced thus.

children.text: atha khalu dakṣiṇā ādiśitavyā /
children.translated_text: Now then, the merit-dedication (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) should be pronounced [thus]:

children.text: sarvvasatvā mariṣyanti maraṇāntaṃ hi jīvitaṃ /
children.translated_text: All beings will die; for life ends in death.

children.text: yathākarmma gamiṣyanti puṇyapāpaphalopagāḥ //
children.translated_text: According to their <s>karma</s> (actions) they will go, experiencing the fruits of merit and sin.

children.text: nirayaṃ pāpakarmmāṇo kṛtapuṇyā ca svarggatiṃ /

children.translated_text: Others, having cultivated the path, attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final liberation), free from defilements.

children.text: (I.p.55) evaṃ dakṣiṇā ādiśitavyā //
children.translated_text: Thus should the merit-dedication be pronounced.

children.translated_text: 'May the wife be gentle, faithful, devoted to her husband and following [him],

children.text: śīlavatī yo(tyā)gasampannā samyagdṛṣṭi ca yā iha /
children.translated_text: virtuous, endowed with renunciation, and of right view here in this world.

children.text: puruṣo pi peśalā bhavatu śrāddho bhavatu vratā(5b5)nugo /
children.translated_text: May the husband too be gentle, faithful, and devoted to his vows,

children.text: śīlavāṃ tyāgasampanno samyagdṛṣṭi ca yo iha //
children.translated_text: virtuous, endowed with renunciation, and of right view here in this world.
Now then, the merit-dedication (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) should be pronounced [thus]:

children.text: ubhau śraddhāya sampannā ubhau śīlo(le)hi saṃvṛtā /
children.translated_text: Both endowed with faith, both restrained by virtue,

children.text: ubhau puṇyāni kṛtvāna samaśīlavratā ubhau //
children.translated_text: both having made merit, both equal in virtue and vows —

children.text: vidhinā devalokas tu modantu kāmakāmino /
children.translated_text: may they, desiring pleasures, rejoice in the world of the gods according to the rite.

children.text: tām eva bhāryāṃ careyā yo asyā sīlehi saṃvṛtā //
children.translated_text: Let him cherish that very wife who is restrained by his virtues.

children.text: asatiṃ parivarjeyā mārggaṃ pratibhayaṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: Let him avoid an unchaste woman, as one [avoids] a dangerous path.'

children.text: evaṃ dakṣiṇā ādiśitavyā //
children.translated_text: Thus should the merit-dedication be pronounced.

children.text:
atha dā(5b6)ni gharapraveśanikaṃ bhavati / nāyaṃ dakṣiṇā ādiśitavyā /
  (J.21) ādīptasmiṃ āgare yo niharati bhaṇḍakaṃ taṃ
  khu tasya svakaṃ bhavati / na khalu yo tatra dahyati /
  evam ādīpite loke mṛtyunā ca jarayā ca
  yo nīharati / dānena dinnaṃ taṃ āhuti hutaṃ /
  nāyaṃ evaṃ dakṣiṇā ādiśitavyā //
children.translated_text:
Now when there is a house-entering [ceremony] (<s>gharapraveśanika</s>), this merit-dedication should not be pronounced:
'When a house is ablaze, whoever carries out goods — those indeed become his own; not indeed [the goods of] one who burns there.
Even so, when the world is ablaze with death and old age,
whoever carries out [merit] by giving — what is given, that is an oblation offered.'
This merit-dedication should not be pronounced thus.

children.text:
atha khalu dakṣiṇā ādiśitavyā
  vibhaktabhāgaṃ ruciraṃ manoramaṃ
  (I.p.56) praśastam ārye[h]i navaṃ nive(5b7)śanaṃ /
  praviśya vṛddhiye varāye bhūrīye
  śirīye lakṣmīparigraheṇa ca /
  imasmi āgāre nivasantu devatāḥ /
  mahābhiṣaṅka na ca anukampikā
  yaṃ vibhavadhanadhānyena sambhavo
  bhūr ime ca sā yasmiṃ pradeśe
medhāvī vā saṃkalpeti paṇḍito
children.translated_text: a wise one or a learned one resolves [to dwell].

children.text: śīlavātantra(n tatra) bhojeyā saṃyatāṃ brahmacāriṇo /
children.translated_text: There one should feed the virtuous, the self-controlled <s>brahmacārins</s> (celibate students).

children.text: (J.22) yā tatra devatā asyā tāsāṃ dakṣiṇām ādiśehi /
children.translated_text: Whatever deities are here, to them you should dedicate the merit-dedication.

children.text: tāye vastumālānāṃ cirarātrāya ka(6a1)lpate //
children.translated_text: For those house-protectors, [this merit] endures for a long time.

Now then, the merit-dedication should be pronounced [thus]:
'With well-apportioned sections, beautiful, delightful,
praised by the noble ones, [this] new dwelling —
having entered, for increase, for the best, for abundance,
for glory, and with the acquisition of <s>Lakṣmī</s> (fortune),
may the deities dwell in this house,
[those of] great consecration and compassion;
whatever prosperity in wealth and grain [there may be],
and may there be abundance in whatever place

children.text: bhojanāvastupālā satkṛtā pratimānitā /
children.translated_text: The guardians of food and dwelling, honored and respected —

children.text: grāme vā yadi vāraṇye nimne vā yadi vā sthale
children.translated_text: whether in a village or in a forest, in a hollow or on a hill,

children.text: divā vā yadi vā rātrau devā rakṣantu dāyakān //
children.translated_text: by day or by night — may the gods protect the donors.'

children.text: devānukampito poṣo sadā bhadrāṇi paśyati //
children.translated_text: One blessed by the gods' compassion always sees auspicious things.

children.text: evaṃ dakṣiṇā ādiśitavyā /
children.translated_text: Thus should the merit-dedication be pronounced.

children.text:
atha dāni gamikaṃ bhaktaṃ bhavati / nāyaṃ dakṣinā ādiśitavyā /
  sarvvā diśāsu bhayā samākulā
sa-uttarā sapurastimā [dakṣi]ṇā paścimā ca
children.translated_text: 'in the north, in the east, in the south, and in the west;'

children.text: sa(6a2)sarvvo ca loko saṃkulajāto
children.translated_text: 'the entire world is born into turmoil —'

children.text: mā pramajji jinaśāsane //
children.translated_text: 'do not be heedless in the teaching of the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror).'

Now when there is a departure-meal (<s>gamika-bhakta</s>), this merit-dedication should not be pronounced:
'In all directions, fears are agitated;'

children.text: nāyaṃ evaṃ dakṣiṇā ādiśitavyā //
children.translated_text: This merit-dedication should not be pronounced thus.

children.text:
atha khalu diśā sauvastikā dakṣiṇā vistareṇa dakṣiṇā ādiśitavyā /
  yathā pātrapratisaṃyukte evaṃ dakṣiṇā ādiśitavyā /
  atha dāni pravrajitasya bhavati / nāyaṃ dakṣiṇā ādiśitavyā
(J.23)putram vā paśum vā ārabhya dhanadhānyapriyāṇi vā
children.translated_text: 'Whether for a son, or for cattle, or for wealth, grain, and loved ones,'

children.text: (I.p.57) devabhāvaṃ vā manuṣyam vā pañcadho (6a3) manasi prīyanti /
children.translated_text: 'or for divine rebirth, or for human [rebirth] — in five ways one delights in the mind.'

children.text: na evaṃ dakṣiṇā ādiśitavyā //
children.translated_text: This merit-dedication should not be pronounced thus.

Now then, the auspicious directional merit-dedication (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) should be pronounced in detail. It should be pronounced as appropriate to the recipient. Now when it is for one gone forth [as a monk], this merit-dedication should not be pronounced:

children.text: atha khalu dakṣiṇā ādiśitavyā /
children.translated_text: Now then, the merit-dedication (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) should be pronounced [thus]:

children.text: suduṣkaraṃ pravrajitasya dānaṃ pātreṇa bhaikṣaṃ abhisāharitvā /
children.translated_text: 'Difficult indeed is the gift to one gone forth, having gathered alms-food with the bowl,

children.text: kulāt kulaṃ cariya piṇḍapātaṃ kruddhaprasannānāṃ mukhaṃ
children.translated_text: wandering from family to family for alms-food, looking upon the faces of the angry and the pleased —

children.text: udīkṣiyaṃ //
children.translated_text: [thus] gazing up.'

children.text:
so yaṃ śreṣṭhāyatane pratiṣṭhito pātrasaṃhṛto lābho prītiṃ janehi
  suvihitā tathā hi dinnaṃ imaṃ dānan ti /
evaṃ dakṣiṇāṃ / (6a4) ādiśiya gantavyaṃ /
children.translated_text: Thus, having pronounced the merit-dedication (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>), one should depart.

children.text: evaṃ saṃghasthavireṇa bhaktāgre pratipadyitavyaṃ / na pratipadyati //
children.translated_text: Thus should the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder conduct himself at the meal-invitation. If he does not so conduct himself,

'That which, established in the best field, is the gain gathered with the bowl — generate joy [in it],
for well-offered indeed is this gift thus given.'

children.text: abhisamācārikāṃ dharmmān atikramati // * //
children.translated_text: he transgresses the rules of proper conduct (<s>abhisamācārika dharma</s>). // * //

children.text:

children.translated_text: The <s>saṃgha</s>-elder too was displeased: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> gives disciplinary action to us,'

children.text:
dvitīyasthavirasya muttikā / āha / āma bhagavan
  bhagavān āha / tena hi evaṃ dvitīyasthavireṇa bhaktāgre
pratipadyitavyaṃ / kin ti dāni dvitīyasthavireṇa bhaktāgre pratipadyitavyaṃ /
children.translated_text:
'[while] the second elder gets off free.' He said: 'Yes, <s>Bhagavān</s>.'
The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Therefore, thus should the second elder conduct himself at the meal-invitation. How then should the second elder conduct himself at the meal-invitation?'

children.text: eṣo dāni koci bhikṣusaṃghaṃ bhaktena nimantrayati / saṃghasthaviro (J.25)
children.translated_text: 'Now when someone invites the <s>bhikṣu</s>-<s>saṃgha</s> to a meal, the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder'

children.text:
na pratibalo bhavati / dvitīyasthavireṇa jānitavyaṃ / ko nimantreti /
bhikṣubhikṣunī upāsakopāsikā āga(6b2)ntuko gamiko vāṇijako

dvāraṃ / sākāraṃ soddeśaṃ pṛcchiya tato dhivāsayitavyaṃ / nāyaṃ
adhivāsitaṃ mayeti / yatrollagnāye āsitavyaṃ /

bhikṣusaṃ,(6b4)gho bhaktena nimantrito kiṃ sidhyati vā kiṃ pacyati vā ti /
yadi tāvad āha / bhante kisya upāsako kahiṃ upāsako ti nāmāsmākaṃ koci

āgacchiyāṇaṃ yadi tāva anugraho bhavati / anugraho sādhitavyo anugraho

children.translated_text:
[If the saṃgha-elder] is not able, the second elder should know: who is making the invitation? Is it a monk, a nun, a male lay follower, a female lay follower, a visitor, a traveler, a merchant, a caravan leader? What is his name? What is his caste? What is the occupation of his parents? In which region is his house? On which street? Which direction does the house face? [Where is] the door of the house? Having asked with details and specifics, then the invitation should be accepted. 'This has not been accepted by me' — one should sit at the designated place.
  If the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder is not able, the second elder, or alternatively one who is on a monthly or fortnightly wandering tour, should be sent, saying: 'Go, find out! In such-and-such a region, on such-and-such a street, a lay follower named so-and-so has invited the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s>; find out what is being prepared and what is being cooked.' Having entered there, he should ask: 'Good health and long life! Is there here [a lay follower] named so-and-so?' The lay follower says: 'Venerable sir, what will you do?' He should say: 'He has invited the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> to a meal; what is being prepared and what is being cooked?' If he says: 'Venerable sir, whose lay follower? Where is this lay follower? We don't know any such lay follower; nothing is being prepared, nothing is being cooked' — then it should be known that the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> has been deceived. Having returned, if there is a substitute provision, the provision should be arranged. If there is no provision, if there are food-tickets, the food-tickets should be distributed. If there are no food-tickets, the bell should be struck with a clanging sound and an announcement made: 'Venerable ones, the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> has been deceived; seek your own individual livelihood.' All should go for alms in order. But if he says: 'Venerable sir, this is prepared, this is cooked; let the venerable assembly enter' — the bell should be struck with a clanging sound and they should enter.
  If it is the winter season, they should enter at a somewhat later time, [for] much time passes [before the food gets cold]. But if it is the summer season, because of the heat, they should enter somewhat earlier. But if it is the rainy season, they should enter between rain showers. Then it is not proper to enter stepping over goods and vessels. Rather, avoiding the goods and vessels, and avoiding boys and girls, one should enter. Then it is not proper to sit down in a passageway. At some seats there, boys and girls might have been put to sleep. Rather, having checked with the hands, avoiding occupied seats, one should sit down. If it is the winter season, time passes quickly [and the food cools fast]. The food-alms should be given first to the sick who remain behind. Now then the lay donors say: 'Venerable sirs, take the food in order.' It should be said: 'No. The <s>Bhagavān</s> has in many ways [praised care for] the sick and afflicted. Should we make the monastery empty [of the sick]? Time passes quickly; give [the food to them] yourselves.' But if it is the summer season or the rainy season, time passes slowly [and the food stays warm]. The food-alms for the sick who remain behind should be received in order. If the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder is not able but the second elder is able, yet it is not proper [to delay], the second elder, eating quickly, having received his portion, should look toward the door, rise, and go.
  Now if the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder is not able but the second elder is able, the second elder should eat, waiting for the best rice to arrive, or waiting for the best side-dishes to arrive. At the time when the junior monks sing chants or drink water or sit with empty hands — then if the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder is not able, the second elder should know: what is the occasion? Is this meal for a birth, a death, a wedding, a house-warming, for a visitor, a traveler, a householder, or a renunciant? According to the occasion, the merit-dedication should be given accordingly. As in the first training-rule, so should the second elder conduct himself at the meal-gathering. Likewise the merit-dedication should be given, and then he should depart. Thus should the second elder conduct himself at the meal-gathering. If he does not so conduct himself, he transgresses the rules of proper conduct (<s>abhisamācārika dharma</s>). // * //

I.5 Ms.6a4 (J.23.12); Ch.499c28 —
The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) was dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, the Teacher of gods and humans.
Having given the background (<s>nidāna</s>) in detail: Now it was the <s>Saṃgha</s>'s external meal [distribution]. The venerable <s>Nandana</s> [was] the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder, <s>Upanandana</s> [was] the second elder. The <s>saṃgha</s>-elder had come, [but] the second elder did not come. The lay donors and patrons asked: 'Venerable one, is the <s>bhikṣu</s>-<s>saṃgha</s> (community of monks) complete?' The <s>bhikṣus</s> said: 'No, long-lived ones.' 'Who then has not come?' They said: 'The second elder has not come.' They then grumbled: 'Look, sirs, we ourselves have left our work and come [to] serve the complete <s>bhikṣu</s>-<s>saṃgha</s> and pay homage at the feet of the venerable ones, [yet] the second elder does not come.' The <s>saṃgha</s>-elder too was displeased: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> gives disciplinary action to us, [while] the second elder gets off free.' The <s>bhikṣus</s> reported this matter to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Summon <s>Upanandana</s>.' He was then summoned. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Is it true, <s>Upanandana</s>, that thus — [when] the <s>Saṃgha</s>'s external meal [was being held], <s>Nandana</s> [was] the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder, you [were] the second elder, the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder had come, the <s>bhikṣus</s> had come, [but] you did not come? The lay donors and patrons asked: "Venerable one, is the <s>bhikṣu</s>-<s>saṃgha</s> complete?" The <s>bhikṣus</s> said: "No." "Who then has not come?" "The second elder has not come." They then grumbled: "We ourselves have left our work and come; we would serve the complete <s>bhikṣu</s>-<s>saṃgha</s> and pay homage at the feet of the venerable ones, [yet] the second elder does not come."

children.translated_text: 'It has been approved by me.' [He should] sit down at the lodging. Now then, if the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder is not capable, [and] the second elder is not capable, whoever is capable, he should naturally send someone on a monthly or fortnightly wandering tour. If perhaps at that place there has been a birth, or a death, or there is danger from the king, or danger from robbers, or danger from wild animals, or danger from storms, and they have invited [monks] with the intention of harassment — he should go there and ask at that house: 'Is there in this [place] a lay devotee or patron or merchant by such-and-such a name?' [If they ask] 'What is this about?' he should say: 'The <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> has been invited by him for a meal.' If they then say: 'There is no one here by such-and-such a name — whose layman [is he]? Whose meal? What kind of meal?' — it should be understood: 'The <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> has been deceived.' Then, having returned, if there is a benefit to be obtained, it should be obtained. [If] there is no benefit, [and if] there are meal-portions, the meal-portions should be assigned. But if there are no meal-portions, the bell should be struck for the alms-round, and all should take their bowls in order and enter [the village] for alms. Now if they say: 'Venerable sir, this much is ready; this much is being cooked,' then having taken the bowls, one should enter. If it is winter time, one should enter following the schedule, [for] the daylight passes quickly.

'Summon the <s>bhikṣus</s>.' They were then summoned. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Is it true, <s>bhikṣus</s>, that thus at the <s>Saṃgha</s>'s external meal, <s>Nandana</s> was the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder, <s>Upanandana</s> the second elder, [they] had come, [but] you came trickling in? The lay donors asked: "Venerable sir, is the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> complete?" The <s>bhikṣus</s> said: "No, long-lived ones." "Who then has not come?" The <s>bhikṣus</s> [said]: "They come trickling in." Then they grumbled: "We ourselves have left our work and come; we will serve the complete <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s>."'

children.translated_text: the lay donors say: 'Venerable sir, take alms food in order for the sick who have stayed behind.' One should say: 'No.' The daylight passes quickly. The <s>Bhagavān</s> has in many ways commended [care for] the sick — 'How could we leave the monastery empty?' But if it is summer or the rainy season, the daylight does not pass quickly. Alms food should be taken in order for the sick who have stayed behind. It is not proper, having eaten whatever was obtained in haste, [then] seeing the door, to get up and leave with the received alms. Now then, if the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder is not capable, [and] the second elder is not capable, whoever is capable there, he should wait for a good preparation of rice, or should eat waiting for a good preparation of side-dishes. He should dedicate the merit. He should ascertain what the occasion is: 'Is this meal for a birth, a death, a wedding, a house-warming, for a guest, for a departing one, for a householder, or for a renunciant?' Then, if it is a birth, the merit should not be dedicated [in the ordinary way]. [Rather, the verse is:] 'This boy, cut from the umbilical cord, survives by the moisture of the thumb; for seven nights dogs and jackals threaten him, and a crow takes the dirt from his eyes.' The merit should not be dedicated in this way.

But if it is summer time, one should enter at the proper time out of concern for the heat. [If it is] the rainy season, one should enter following the schedule between rain showers. Furthermore, it is not proper to enter stepping over goods, or to enter stepping over vessels, or to enter stepping over boys and girls. Rather, one should enter going around the goods, going around the boys and girls. Furthermore, it is not proper for those who have entered to sit wherever there is room. Sometimes at that place the seats may have pregnant women lying upon them, or vessels may have been placed [on them]. Rather, having examined [each seat] by hand, avoiding the seats of those in the immediate [birthing] period, one should sit down in order of seniority. Then, if it is winter time, the daylight passes quickly.

children.translated_text: nor teach [them].' Therefore, thus should the preceptor conduct himself toward [his] co-resident pupil (<s>sārddhavihārin</s>). And how should the preceptor conduct himself toward [his] co-resident pupil? The preceptor, when about to ordain a co-resident pupil, should first have him learn both <s>Vinayas</s> (monastic disciplines). If he cannot master both <s>Vinayas</s>, he should have him learn one <s>Vinaya</s>. If he cannot master one <s>Vinaya</s>, he should have him learn five <s>sūtras</s> in detail. If he cannot master five <s>sūtras</s>, then four, or three, or two, or one <s>sūtra</s> should be learned in detail. If he cannot master even one <s>sūtra</s>, he should have him learn the thirty [rules] as well — the remainder being the verses for frequent recitation. If he cannot master even the thirty, he should have him learn the two <s>aniyatas</s> (undetermined rules) — the remainder being the verses for frequent recitation. If he cannot master the two <s>aniyatas</s>, at the very least he should have him learn the four <s>pārājikas</s> (offences of defeat) — the remainder being the verses for frequent recitation — and should train him. He should instruct him morning, midday, and evening — in the evening with <s>Abhidharma</s> (higher doctrine) or <s>Abhivinaya</s> (higher discipline). <s>Abhidharma</s> means the ninefold <s>sūtrānta</s> (discourses): <s>sūtra</s>, <s>geya</s> (mixed prose and verse), <s>vyākaraṇa</s> (explanation), <s>gāthā</s> (verse), <s>udāna</s> (inspired utterance), <s>itivṛttaka</s> (narrative), <s>jātaka</s> (birth story), <s>vaipulya</s> (extensive discourse), and <s>adbhutadharma</s> (marvelous phenomena). <s>Abhivinaya</s> means the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> (monastic code) in its condensed and detailed divisions. But if he is not capable of reciting [it all], he should be trained in skill regarding offences (<s>āpattikauśalya</s>), skill in <s>sūtras</s>, skill in the aggregates (<s>skandhakauśalya</s>), skill in the sense-bases (<s>āyatanakauśalya</s>), skill in dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpādakauśalya</s>), and skill in what is possible and impossible (<s>sthānāsthānakauśalya</s>). He should be trained in proper conduct and restrained from improper conduct. Now if he instructs [the pupil], that itself is his instruction — thus he studies, he dwells in the forest, he sits in meditation. That itself is his instruction. [But if] the preceptor, having ordained a co-resident pupil, does not instruct, does not teach, does not recite, does not study, does not dwell in the forest, does not sit in meditation — at the very least he should be told: 'Practice with diligence!' If he does not instruct, he incurs a transgression of the <s>Vinaya</s>. Thus should the preceptor conduct himself toward [his] co-resident pupil. If he does not so conduct himself, he transgresses the rules of proper conduct (<s>abhisamācārika dharma</s>). //*//

I.7 Ms.8a5 (J. 33.5); Ch.501c14 — The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, the Teacher of gods and humans. Having given the background in detail: Now the venerable <s>Nandana</s> and <s>Upanandana</s> and the group-of-six [monks] were ordaining [new monks]. Having ordained [them], they did not instruct them, they did not teach them. They let them grow like <s>indragava</s> (wild plants); they raised them like wild goats. [The new monks were] not properly equipped, not accomplished in deportment. They did not know: how should one conduct oneself toward the preceptor? How should one conduct oneself toward the teacher? How should one conduct oneself toward the senior monks? How should one conduct oneself in the midst of the <s>saṃgha</s>? How should one conduct oneself in the village? How should one conduct oneself in the forest? How should one wear the [inner] robe? How should one put on the outer robe? How should one conduct oneself regarding the wearing of the <s>saṃghāṭī</s> (triple robe), bowl, and [other] robes?

A small lamp should be lit.
If there is alms-food [that has been brought back], it should be offered [to the preceptor]. If it is of unusual appearance, [the pupil] should be asked: 'Well-situated one, where was this obtained?' [If he says] 'From such-and-such a courtesan's family, from a widow, from a mature girl, from a <s>paṇḍaka</s> (eunuch), from such-and-such a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> (nun)' — [if] he indicates households that are suspect and questionable — he should be restrained, told: 'Do not go there.' But if he then says: 'In such-and-such a family the word of the <s>Buddha</s> was spoken; it was obtained from there' — he should be told: 'Make smoke [to purify it], and do not again look with greedy eyes.' Having washed the hands, hand-washing water should be given. The alms-food should be set out; the alms-food should be offered. While [the preceptor is] eating, drinking water should be served. Fan-breeze should be given. The meal-dismissal should be announced. After he has eaten and entered, the bowl should be removed. And the vessels, food-rest, and bedding should be put away. The robes and bowl should be cleaned. The bowl should be stored. The dwelling should be sprinkled and swept. From time to time cow-dung plaster should be applied. The bedding should be beaten and aired. The robes should be washed, rinsed, and dyed. The bowl should be fired and treated. When [the preceptor] goes for day-rest, a stool should be brought, a sitting-cloth should be brought, a book should be brought, a water-pot should be brought. Having taken the lesson, one should sit aside studying. Now if [the pupil] wishes to go for day-rest, he should take leave before going. If he wishes to study together with someone there, he should ask permission, saying: 'I will study with so-and-so.' The [preceptor] should then know: if that one is lax, or indolent, or decadent, or unwilling to learn, he should be told: 'Lest bad association arise [do not].' But if he is good, virtuous, and eager to learn, he should be told: 'Do so.' When [the preceptor] returns from day-rest, a stool should be brought, a sitting-cloth should be brought, a book should be brought, a water-pot should be brought. When he has arrived, hand-washing water should be given, flowers should be given. When he goes to pay respects at the <s>caitya</s> (shrine), [the pupil] should follow behind. A stool should be prepared. If it is winter time, a small lamp should be lit. The feet should be washed. The feet should be anointed. The bed should be prepared. If there are many people, at the very least the arrangement should be made by hand. A lamp should be lit. A spittoon should be offered. A urinal should be offered. He should be made comfortable for retiring. Having inquired and asked, if a dwelling is obtained, he should take leave: 'I take such-and-such a dwelling.' But if he obtains a dwelling with a second person, the preceptor (<s>upādhyāya</s>) should know: if that one is lax, or indolent, or decadent, or unwilling to learn,

But when he is expelled, he should take leave each time [he receives] a penance. If he wishes to study together with someone there, he should ask permission: 'I will study with so-and-so.' The preceptor (<s>upādhyāya</s>) should know [about this]. Thus should the co-resident (<s>sārddhavihārin</s>) conduct himself toward the preceptor. I.10 Ms.10a3 (J.41:6); Ch.502b16 —
The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, the Teacher of gods and humans. Having given the background (<s>nidāna</s>) in detail: Now those monks gave dependence (<s>niśraya</s>). Those pupils, having received the teacher's dependence, neither attended upon [him] nor showed respect. Those monks then became displeased: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> gives disciplinary action to us, [while] these get off free — who neither attend upon us nor show respect. How are we to instruct and teach them?' The monks reported this matter to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Summon the monks.' They were then summoned.
The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Therefore, thus should the pupil (<s>antevāsin</s>) conduct himself toward the teacher (<s>ācārya</s>). The pupil, rising early in the morning, should knock at the door of the teacher's dwelling. When permission is given, the door [should be opened] gently without slamming. First the right foot should be entered, then entering the left foot, [he should wish] the teacher 'a pleasant night'

walking around and inspecting. What five? [To check:] 'Are my disciples not delighting in work, not attached to work, not dwelling devoted to the pursuit of delight in work? Are they not delighting in talk, not attached to talk, not dwelling devoted to the pursuit of delight in talk? Are they not delighting in sleep, not attached to sleep, not dwelling devoted to the pursuit of delight in sleep?' And for the sake of compassion for sick monks. And [so that] those faithful sons of good family who have gone forth from home into homelessness with faith, specifically for the sake of the <s>Tathāgata</s> — they, having seen the <s>Tathāgata</s>, will obtain exceedingly lofty joy and delight. Seeing these five reasons, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly and fully awakened ones undertake the five-day monastery inspection tour, walking around and inspecting. The <s>Bhagavān</s> saw, while walking around and inspecting on the five-day monastery tour, bedding and seats that were abandoned and scattered, raised up and bumpy, being destroyed by wind and sun, being rained on by rain, being eaten by insects, being soiled by birds — dirty and stained, torn and ripped, placed out in the sun. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, though knowing, asked the monks: 'Whose is this bedding and seating that is abandoned and scattered,' and so forth in abbreviated form, 'up to dirty and stained, torn and ripped, placed out in the sun?' They said: 'This, <s>Bhagavān</s>, belongs to the <s>Saṃgha</s>.'
The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Thus you use the communal bedding and seats without spreading-covers! Therefore, one should conduct oneself thus regarding bedding and seats. And how should one conduct oneself regarding bedding and seats? children.translated_text: it should be gathered up and placed to one side. If it is bumpy, it should be leveled. If it is being rained on by rain or being destroyed by wind and sun, it should be brought under cover. If it is being eaten by insects or being soiled by birds, it should be shaken out and brought under cover. Furthermore, the monastery should not be neglected — [whether it is] dilapidated, crumbling, unsightly, or unrepaired. Now if it has a grass roof, grass bundles should be provided. If it has a bark roof, bark should be provided. If it has a tile roof, tiles should be provided. If it has a plaster-and-clay roof, clay lumps should be provided. If it has been flooded by rain, the puddles should be filled in, a broom should be provided, and a cow-dung plaster should be applied. Furthermore, it is not proper to use communal bedding and seats in this way — without a spreading-cover, or with [just] grass interposed, or with a reed mat. Rather, a spreading-cover should be made. Nor is it proper to make a spreading-cover of [fine] cloth or canvas. Rather, a double-folded [cover] should be made, larger than the bed. If it is of wool, one or two layers should be made. But if it is of cotton, two or three layers should be made, sewn all around with thread in a quilted pattern. Then lengthwise threads should be inserted in the middle. Furthermore, it is not proper to neglect bedding and seats [that are] dirty and stained, or torn and ripped. Rather, from time to time they should be washed; from time to time they should be sprinkled; from time to time they should be placed in the sun. It is not proper to sit at the meal-invitation, or the refreshment session, or the community assembly while wrapped in communal bedding. It is not proper to walk the long walkway while wearing communal bedding as a wrap. But if a monk has had a bloodletting, or has taken a purgative, or is ill, having placed a personal cloth as an interposing [layer], he may walk about — there is no offence. Furthermore, it is not proper to use communal bedding for personal use. Rather, communal bedding should be set out, and having placed a spreading-cover, one should use it. Now if the communal bedding is large, one should use it from above so that it does not come to ruin. Now if it is winter time and one sleeps wrapped in communal bedding, an interposing [cloth] should be placed [between]. If one does not provide [it], one incurs a transgression of the <s>Vinaya</s>. Thus should one conduct oneself regarding bedding and seats. If one does not so conduct oneself, one transgresses the rules of proper conduct (<s>abhisamācārika dharma</s>). //*//

<s>Bhagavān</s>, belong to the <s>Saṃgha</s>. Those who will take up the rainy-season [retreat] will repair them.'
  The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Therefore, one should conduct oneself thus regarding lodgings at the approach of the rains. And how should one conduct oneself regarding lodgings at the approach of the rains? Now when it is the <s>Saṃgha</s>'s approach-of-the-rains [season], first the lay donors should be visited. Then the monastery dwellings should be repaired. Those dwellings that are dilapidated or broken, dirty or unrepaired: if it has a plaster roof, a ball of plaster should be given; if it has a brick roof, bricks should be given; if it has a tile roof, tiles should be given; if it has a potsherd roof, potsherds should be given; if it has a thatch roof, bundles of thatch should be given. If the beds or seats are dilapidated or broken, <s>muñja</s> grass should be cut, <s>balbaja</s> grass should be cut, and beds should be restrung. If they are wobbly, they should be steadied properly. If they are badly set up, they should be properly set up. If they are filled with wind and sun, or defecated upon by crows and birds, they should be placed under shelter. As for the bedding that is soiled and torn, it should be washed and sewn. Balls of clay should be provided. Rat holes and cavities should be filled in. Whatever goods belonging [to the community] are in the precincts, all should be gathered together.
  A <s>bhikṣu</s> endowed with five qualities should be appointed by the <s>Saṃgha</s> as the lodging-allocator. Which five? One who acts without favoritism, without hatred, without delusion, without fear, and who knows what has been allocated and what has not. With these five [qualities]. Abbreviated.

II.2 Ms. 11a4 (J.47.6); Ch.502c13 — The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, the Teacher of gods and humans. Having given the background in detail: Now those monks did not repair the monastery at the time of the approaching [rains]. Seeing five reasons, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly and fully awakened ones undertake the five-day monastery inspection tour, walking around and inspecting. What five? [To check:] 'Are my disciples not delighting in work, not attached to work, not dwelling devoted to the pursuit of delight in work? Are they not delighting in talk, not attached to talk, not dwelling devoted to the pursuit of delight in talk? Are they not delighting in sleep, not attached to sleep, not dwelling devoted to the pursuit of delight in sleep?' And for the sake of compassion for sick monks. And [so that] those faithful sons of good family who have gone forth from home into homelessness with faith, specifically for the sake of the <s>Tathāgata</s> — they, having seen the <s>Tathāgata</s>, will obtain exceedingly lofty joy and delight. Seeing these five reasons, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly and fully awakened ones undertake the five-day monastery inspection tour, walking around and inspecting.

Having performed the formal act, then around the month of <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, lodgings should be allocated. Monasteries, precincts, fire-halls, dining halls, service halls, gate-rooms, latrines, wells, bath-houses, walking paths, tree-roots — all monastery dwellings should be allocated. 'In such-and-such a monastery, there are this many beds, this many seats, this much bedding, this many coverings' — this should be written on birch-bark, on a board, or on a strip of cloth. If it is a forest lodging and the precincts are far away, on the thirteenth or fourteenth day the lodging assignment should be made. But if it is a village-adjacent lodging and the precincts are nearby, on the fourteenth or fifteenth day the lodging assignment should be made. That written record should be presented to the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder, saying: 'Venerable one, in such-and-such a monastery there are this many beds, this many seats, this much bedding, this many coverings — which monastery pleases you?' Whichever monastery pleases the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder, that should be given to him. But if the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder says: 'You assign the dwellings; we will make the rainy-season [arrangements] equal' — as the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder says, so it should be done. Then the dwellings should be assigned, beginning from the most senior down to the most junior. It is not proper to assign dwellings to <s>śrāmaṇeras</s> (novices). But if their preceptors and teachers say: 'Assign [dwellings] to these; we will repair [them]' — then dwellings should be assigned to the <s>śrāmaṇeras</s> too. But if there are many [monks], then a second allocation should be made. But if there is someone who roars the lion's roar [i.e., one competent in disputes], sufficient for summer, lodgings should be assigned for safekeeping and for use, [noting] what is to be removed and what is to be set up. 'Which monastery?' It should be said: 'This is not for any [personal] enjoyment; they will say it is for repair purposes; that is why it is being assigned.' If the dwellings are few, one dwelling should be assigned for two or three persons. If even thus they are few, one dwelling should be assigned for four or five persons. If there is only one dwelling and the <s>bhikṣus</s> are many, beds should be allocated for the senior monks, seats for the junior monks. If even thus there are few, seats should be allocated for the seniors, mats for the juniors. If even thus there are few and the space is limited, the seniors should use mats, the juniors should make do with sleeping places [on the ground]. If even thus the space is limited, the seniors should enter the sheltered area, the juniors should make do at tree-roots, walking paths, sitting areas, or in the open air. In winter, lodgings should be assigned for safekeeping, for use, for removing and being removed. In the rainy season, lodgings should be assigned for safekeeping, for use, for removing and being removed. It is not proper to neglect the lodgings when they are soiled and torn, or when the beds and seats are dilapidated or broken. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Therefore, thus should those who have entered the rains-retreat (<s>varṣopagata</s>) conduct themselves regarding bedding and seats. And how should those who have entered the rains-retreat conduct themselves regarding bedding and seats? These monks have now entered the rains-retreat. Therefore, the dwellings should be inspected. If they are dilapidated or crumbling, up to: rat-droppings or puddles should be repaired. If the dwelling has a plaster roof, a plaster lump should be provided. If it has a brick roof, bricks should be provided. If it has a bark roof, bark should be provided. If it has a tile roof, tiles should be provided. If it has a grass roof, grass bundles should be provided. If [the wall] has been grabbed by creepers, it should be stripped and plastered with clay. Rat-droppings and puddles should be filled in. If the dwelling has cracks, they should be filled with gravel or unbaked clay-dust. But if it is dusty, a cow-dung layer should be applied. Water channels or drain channels that have become blocked should be cleaned out. Flat-roofed upper chambers should be repaired. If the bedding is dirty and stained, or torn and ripped, it should be washed and dyed. If beds or stools are broken, the broken joints should be repaired. If they are dilapidated or crumbling, rushes should be cut; beds should be re-strung; stools should be re-strung. If [the legs] are uneven, they should be leveled. If they are wobbly, they should be made firm. If they are damaged by wind and sun, awnings should be placed. If they are rained upon by rain, they should be placed under cover. If they are eaten by insects, they should be placed on raised supports for drying. Furthermore, it is not proper to neglect bedding and seats [that are] dirty and stained, or torn and ripped. Rather, from time to time they should be washed, sewn, and dyed. If beds or stools are uneven, they should be leveled. If they are wobbly, they should be made firm. If they are dilapidated or crumbling, rushes should be cut, <s>balbaja</s> grass should be cut, beds should be re-strung, stools should be re-strung. If the legs are wobbly, they should be made firm. The dwellings should be sprinkled from time to time, swept, and given a cow-dung layer. Water channels or drain channels should be cleaned from time to time. Every five days the bedding should be aired in the sun. Beds or stools should be turned to different positions. If the dwelling is damp, the bed should be detached from the wall and given supports, so that [the bedding] is not eaten by insects. A covering-cloth should be applied. Every half-month a cow-dung layer should be applied. If the dwelling becomes moist, water should be [drained out]. But if it becomes sweaty [with condensation], it should be rubbed with clean cow-dung. If the dwelling is sweaty, it is not proper there to wash the hands, or wash the feet, or wash the face, or clean the feet. Nor is it proper to shut the dwelling and leave it. Rather, from time to time it should be opened so that it gets air. It should be fumigated with <s>kuṣṭha</s> (costus root), birch bark, or barley flour. Thus should those who have entered the rains-retreat conduct themselves regarding bedding and seats. If they do not so conduct themselves, they transgress the rules of proper conduct (<s>abhisamācārika dharma</s>). //*//

II.3 Ms.12a6 (J.52.15); Ch.503a24 — The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>. The Teacher of gods and humans — having given the <s>nidāna</s> (narrative occasion) in full — up to: the <s>Bhagavān</s> saw, on his five-day tour of the monastery dwellings, walking about and inspecting — the dwellings dilapidated, broken, taken over by lizards, dirty, unrepaired, full of water, the water channels uncleaned, being gnawed at the doors by lizards, the beds and seats dilapidated, broken, fallen over, being rained upon, being eaten by insects. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing, asked: 'What [is the state of] these, <s>bhikṣus</s>? The dwellings are hanging loose, taken over by lizards, dirty, unrepaired, full of water, the water channels uncleaned, being gnawed at the doors by lizards, the beds and seats dilapidated, broken, wobbly, fallen over, being rained upon by rain, being eaten by insects'

children.translated_text: Equipment should be prepared; a white-wash should be applied. All around the monastery, as a matter of course, a firebreak should be made. With hired workers and laborers, whatever undergrowth has grown on the four sides of the monastery should be cut down. When it is dry and free of living creatures, it should be burned with fire. The dwelling should be sprinkled, swept, and given a cow-dung layer. Whatever essential bedding — whether quilts, or coverlets, or cushions, or pillows, or bolsters, or small cushions — should be brought to the village-adjacent quarters. The beds should be placed on supports, attached to the wall. On top of the beds, the stools should be placed. On top of the stools, whatever bedding is dirty and stained, or torn and ripped, should be placed on top of the stools and placed on the robe-rack, detached from the wall. If the dwelling has cracks, it is not proper to seal [the openings]. Rather, they should be left open. But if the dwellings are dusty, outer enclosures should be made. Everyone should clear out [the dwelling]; one person should make an inner enclosure and descend by rope or ladder. Having descended, the rope or ladder should be thrown inside, or pulled from outside. Whatever cowherds or shepherds are there, that dwelling should be entrusted to them. They should be told: 'Long-lived ones, we are going now to the village-adjacent quarters. May this your monastery be kept in trust.' Having thus entrusted it, one should go. II.4 Ms.13a1 (J. 56.3); Ch.503b10 — The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, the Teacher of gods and humans. Having given the background in detail: Now the forest-dwelling bedding and seats — due to the danger of snow, the mind does not dwell [there comfortably]. Those forest-dwelling monks, having had an outer enclosure made for the dwelling, moved down to the village-adjacent quarters. Then that dwelling was burned when a forest fire came. The monks reported this matter to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Therefore, thus should those who have completed the rains-retreat (<s>varṣavusta</s>) conduct themselves regarding bedding and seats. And how should those who have completed the rains-retreat conduct themselves regarding bedding and seats? These forest-dwelling bedding and seats — due to the danger of snow, [one's] mind does not dwell [there]. It is not proper for the forest-dwellers to move down to a village-adjacent quarter without notice. Rather, [some] should be encouraged [to stay]. One, or two, or three there — as many as are willing — whoever is capable of staying, if they are willing, their food should be supported so that they are not abandoned. But if they protest, saying: "What, are we abandoned? Why should we stay?" — whatever bedding and seats are there — cushions, pillows, square mats, water-jars, or bowls — everything should be brought down to the village-adjacent quarters. The beds and stools should be lifted up and stored. The beds should be detached from the walls and given supports so that they are not eaten by insects or termites. Furthermore, it is not proper to neglect that dwelling — [whether it is] dilapidated, crumbling, unsightly, or unrepaired. Rather, if it has a grass roof,

children.translated_text: And how should visiting monks conduct themselves regarding lodgings? Now those <s>bhikṣus</s> are visitors, and the monastery is designated [to someone]. The bed, stool, square cushion, brush, and pillow are designated [to someone]. It is not proper for one merely coming and going to bring goods into the monastery. Rather, if the monastery is dark, a lamp should be lit, or a grass-torch or a stalk-torch should be lit. Having entered, the robe-rack should be examined, for sometimes it has been eaten by insects. II.5 Ms.13b6 (J. 60.5); Ch.503c1 — The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, the Teacher of gods and humans. Having given the background in detail and the five reasons in detail: The <s>Bhagavān</s>, on the five-day monastery inspection tour, walking around and inspecting, saw monasteries that were crumbling, dilapidated, unclean, and unrepaired; lodgings abandoned and scattered, tangled, torn and ripped; beds and stools crumbling, dilapidated, splitting, and tilting; being rained on by rain, being eaten by insects. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing, asked the <s>bhikṣus</s>: "Why are these monasteries, <s>bhikṣus</s>, crumbling, dilapidated, unclean, and unrepaired? The lodgings abandoned and scattered, tangled, torn and ripped? The beds and stools crumbling, dilapidated, splitting, and tilting? Being rained on by rain, being eaten by insects?"

children.translated_text: What is broken or cracked should be repaired. The bedding should be washed, sewn, and dyed. If beds or stools are broken, the knots should be retied. If they are sagging or falling apart, <s>muñja</s> (rush grass) should be cut, <s>balbaja</s> (coarse grass) should be cut, beds should be re-strung, stools should be re-strung. If beds or stools are uneven, they should be placed level. If they are wobbly, they should be made firm. If they are filled with wind and sun, they should be placed in a sheltered spot. If they are soiled by crows and birds, they should be placed under cover. If they are rained upon, they should be placed out of the rain. If they are eaten by insects, the knots should be retied and they should be placed on supports. Thus should the resident monks conduct themselves regarding the bedding. If they do not so conduct themselves, they transgress the rules of proper conduct (<s>abhisamācārika dharma</s>). // * //

II.6 Ms.14a5 (J.62.4); Ch.503c16 — The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, the Teacher of gods and humans. Having given the background in detail and the five reasons in detail: The <s>Bhagavān</s>, on the five-day monastery inspection tour, walking around and inspecting, saw monasteries crumbling, dilapidated, unclean, and unrepaired; lodgings tangled, torn and ripped; beds and stools crumbling, dilapidated, splitting, and tilting; being rained on by rain, being eaten by insects. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing, asked: "Why are these monasteries, <s>bhikṣus</s>, crumbling, dilapidated, unclean, and unrepaired? The lodgings tangled, torn and ripped? The beds and stools crumbling, dilapidated, splitting, and tilting? Being rained on by rain, being eaten by insects?" The <s>bhikṣus</s> said: "We, <s>Bhagavān</s>, are residents; those who are visitors, they will repair [them]." The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Therefore, thus resident monks should conduct themselves regarding lodgings. And how should resident monks conduct themselves regarding lodgings? It is not proper for resident monks to assign to visiting monks monasteries that are crumbling, dilapidated, unclean, and unrepaired — [thinking:] 'If there is urgent need for the visitors, they will repair them.' Rather, monasteries that are new and well-repaired should be assigned to visiting monks. And it is not proper to assign to visiting monks lodgings that are tangled, torn, and ripped — [thinking:] 'If there is urgent need for the visitors, they will wash, dye, and sew them.' Rather, lodgings that are new, well-washed, and well-dyed should be assigned to visiting monks. And it is not proper to assign to visiting monks beds or stools that are dilapidated or crumbling — [thinking:] 'If there is urgent need for the visitors, they will re-weave them.' Rather, beds or stools that are new, strong, and well-cleaned should be assigned to visiting monks. And it is not proper

II.7 Ms.14b5 (J.64.6); Ch.503c25 —
The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, the Teacher of gods and humans. Having given the background in detail: The <s>Bhagavān</s>, while walking on a five-day tour of inspection through the dwellings, saw the dwellings sagging and falling apart, unrepaired, with plaster peeling off; the bedding soiled and dirty, torn and ripped; the beds and stools sagging, falling apart, uneven, wobbly, filled with wind and sun, soiled by crows and birds, rained upon, eaten by insects. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, though knowing, asked the monks: 'Why are these dwellings sagging and falling apart, the bedding soiled and dirty, torn and ripped, the beds and stools sagging, falling apart, uneven, wobbly, filled with wind and sun, soiled by crows and birds, rained upon, eaten by insects?' The monks said: 'Whichever visiting or resident monks [are here], <s>Bhagavān</s>, they will repair them. We are only temporary residents.'
The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Therefore, thus should all conduct themselves regarding the bedding. How then should all conduct themselves regarding the bedding? These dwellings are sagging, falling apart, unclean, unrepaired — therefore, at the sound of the bell, the entire <s>saṃgha</s> should assemble. Now if anyone says: "I am a <s>dharmakathika</s> (Dharma-preacher), I am a <s>vinayadhara</s> (Vinaya-expert), I am a forest-dweller, an alms-collector, a rag-robe wearer — let those menial monks repair them" — they incur a <s>Vinaya</s> transgression.
Rather, all should assemble. Some should knead clay; others should fill and bring bricks, clods, or lumps; others should carry [materials]; others should plaster; others should smooth; others should carry water. Now if there is much to be plastered and the monks work sluggishly, what should be done? Measured portions should be assigned: "This section is yours, this section is yours" — "This must be repaired by you." These dwellings whose plaster has peeled off, that are unrepaired or dusty — having struck the bell for the entire <s>saṃgha</s>, some should strip off the old peeling plaster from the walls; others should knead clay; others should carry water; others should carry clay; others should apply the coating; others should sweep. If the dwellings have damaged floors — gravel or wind-blown dust should be carried [away] and [the floor] should be tamped down. Now if the dwellings are dusty, some should carry cow-dung; others should carry water; others should spread [the mixture]; others should apply the cow-dung plaster. Nor should [this] be neglected. The bedding — whether quilts, blankets, covers, cushions, square mats, pillows, or curtains — [if] soiled, dirty, torn, ripped, unclean, or unrepaired, then from time to time some should strain the lye-wash; others should carry water; others should bring alkali; others should wash [them]; others should wring [them]; others should spread [them] out; others should carry [them back]. If beds or stools are sagging or falling apart, all should cut <s>muñja</s> or <s>balbaja</s> grass; beds should be re-strung, stools should be re-strung, cushions should be sewn, square mats should be stitched, and the frames should be raised. children.translated_text: be filled. From time to time they should be washed. From time to time they should be dried in the sun. But if those are made of wood, it is not proper to dry them in the sun, lest they crack. Having dried them, they should be placed in the shade. When they are completely dry, then they should be filled [again]. In front of the latrine, a hut or hall should be built. There, robe-poles, robe-pegs, or long elephant-tusk hooks should be made, where the <s>bhikṣus</s> may set aside their proper robes before entering the latrine. It is not proper, as a Dravidian would, to take the cleaning vessel and go to the waste-pot. If the waste-pot contains living beings, it is not proper to say: 'Venerable ones, the waste-pot has living beings.' Rather, grass or cotton should be placed on top as a sign that it contains living beings. When attending to water-needs, one should not splash the water carelessly. Rather, one should pour gently. When one sees an empty waste-pot, one should not neglect it. If someone has a helper, it should be reported to him. Otherwise one should fill it oneself. At minimum, in the pot, as much as would serve one person should be provided. But if one is sick, suffering from hemorrhoids or diarrhea, one should be cared for with cloth strips or bellows-cloths or soft materials.

II.8 Ms.15a7 (J.67.9); Ch.504a14 —
The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, the Teacher of gods and humans. Having given the background in detail: Now the monks were relieving themselves in the open. The people then grumbled: 'Look, sirs, these ascetics — like camels, or oxen, or donkeys, or goats — just so these ascetics relieve themselves in the open. [They are] depraved and fallen; how can they [claim] the ascetic life?' The monks heard this matter; the monks reported [it] to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Is it true, monks, that the people grumble [thus]?' 'Yes, <s>Bhagavān</s>.'
The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Therefore, a latrine (<s>varccakuṭī</s>) should be built. Now when a monk is having a latrine built, it is not proper to have it built to the east or to the north of the dwelling. Rather, it should be built to the south or to the west, away from the wind-path. A pit should be dug on hard, brick-like ground. If it is on a slope or near water, first a proper [channel] should be dug out. Now if it is on a slope and [the waste] goes toward a wool-washing shed, a beam should be placed across. First, a round or square [frame] should be fitted and [it should be] covered with bricks or stones. Whatever timbers are solid, strong, and thick — those should be placed underneath. There, [it should be covered] with timbers or planks. On top, [it should be] covered with bricks and clay. Openings should be made, one cubit in length and a fist's width minus [the width of the fist]. There, waist-high or neck-high partitions should be made with bamboo, or reeds, or frames, or planks — constructed such that those seated cannot see one another. A roof should be placed over the top, a wall should be raised, [and] a ridge-beam [should be set].

children.translated_text: * // This is the origination of the matter. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>. The Teacher of gods and humans — having given the <s>nidāna</s> (narrative occasion) in full — now a certain <s>bhikṣu</s> scratched a wound opening with bamboo splinters, causing injury and bleeding. The <s>bhikṣus</s> reported this matter to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Summon the <s>bhikṣu</s>.' He was summoned. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'So you scratched a wound opening with bamboo splinters. Therefore, it is not proper to scratch a wound opening with bamboo splinters, or with split bamboo pieces, or with reed-wood, or with a scraper, or with bone fragments. Rather, a cleansing stick should be made. Or a suppository should be placed. A clay stick should be made. If the latrine is a pit-latrine, it is not proper for a <s>bhikṣu</s> cleaning a wound to throw those sticks or suppositories into the latrine. Rather, a pile should be made to one side. Those should be removed daily, or burned and replaced. But if a <s>bhikṣu</s> sees [and thinks]: "Who will burn these?" — those should be removed and others placed. But if it is situated near a precipice, even if one throws cleansing materials or refuse there, there is no offence. When defecating, one should do so in such a way that feces, urine, spit, and nasal mucus all go into [the pit]. But if another has cleaned [the area], and phlegm, spit, nasal mucus, or feces has been deposited there, all should be thrown into the pit. It is not proper, without having attended to water-needs, to use the <s>Saṃgha</s>'s bedding and seats. * // This is the origination of the matter.'
